original_test_intent: Deploy the approved BlueField BFB to the exact DPU through rshim, update the intended NIC/DPU firmware, activate it by the approved reboot/power cycle and verify the resulting firmware version.
original_method: Map BlueField serial/SKU to rshim0 and its DPU mmc target; verify signed BFB/firmware checksums and compatibility; preserve baseline; approve bf.cfg/NIC-FW, bfb-install, force updater and reboot as separate phases; monitor power/OOB; collect full phase logs and verify exact post-boot versions and services.
manual_activity: DPU owner supplies signed artifacts and exact target map, validates recovery/power/OOB and approves each destructive phase; operator owns physical recovery and verdict.
required_inputs: Signed BFB/DOCA/firmware files with checksums and compatibility recipe
BlueField serial/SKU to rshim0 and mmc target mapping
Approved NIC firmware update and force-update scope
Stable redundant power plus OOB/console and maintenance isolation
Backup/rollback/vendor recovery plan and exact expected versions
safety_requirements: Never infer rshim or mmc target
Authorize BFB write, NIC-FW update, forced updater and reboot separately
Preserve complete flash and system logs
Stop on target, signature, write, link, power or recovery anomaly; no auto-retry
agent_execution_scope: Execute only the currently allowlisted phase
Stop and escalate before any unapproved retry
engineer_actions: Approve artifact and exact destructive targets
Approve each flash/reboot phase and recovery

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Generic remote lspci/devlink does not execute or prove the source rshim BFB, NIC-FW, forced update and reboot sequence; sshpass and truncation are rejected.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use vendor-supported rshim/bfb-install/updater commands only after exact target/artifact verification, recording each command, exit and device state; finish with full bfvcheck/lspci/devlink.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The stated rshim0, mmcblk0, NIC-FW update, forced firmware update, reboot and 15-minute allocations are preserved pending engineering feasibility review.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat the BFB deployment as a signed, target-bound, phase-gated firmware transaction with health stops and vendor recovery ready.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds provenance, target attestation, no-clear evidence, power/OOB gates and per-phase approval.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Read-only enumeration cannot substitute for the intended BFB/NIC firmware transition.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong target/image or interrupted write can brick the DPU, sever networking or strand the host.

project_override_considerations: DPU/vendor owner must approve whether WITH_NIC_FW_UPDATE and forced updater are both required, correct reboot versus chassis power cycle, expected versions and supported recovery for this SKU.
expected_evidence: Complete bf.cfg, bfb-install, updater and reboot outputs/exits

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: DeepSeek is incomplete and insecure but recognizes the same BFB/firmware/reboot intent; the Master remains authoritative for the omitted destructive phases.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Static review is complete; execution blocks if signed artifacts, exact rshim/mmc/NIC-FW mapping, force scope, stable power/OOB or tested recovery are unavailable.

review_improvement: Makes every irreversible target and transition explicit instead of treating a generic enumeration check as proof of a successful BFB deployment.
independent_technical_reasoning: BFB installation, NIC firmware update and a forced firmware updater are separate writes with different failure domains; a successful final lspci alone cannot prove each happened to the intended DPU. Target attestation, phase logs and recovery readiness are therefore mandatory.
